title_en: Yadgar-e-Ghalib, Part One: The Life of Ghalib
author: Altaf Hussain Hali
edition: First edition, Nami Press, Kanpur, 1897. Part One (Hali's life of Ghalib, pp. 1-105) only; Part Two, the anthology, is not included.
description: Altaf Husain Hali's Yadgar-e-Ghalib (1897) is the first full biography of Mirza Asadullah Khan Ghalib (1797–1869), the greatest poet of Urdu and the last great Persian poet of India, written by a younger poet who knew him in his last years. This edition gives the whole of Part One, Hali's life of Ghalib: his Turkish ancestry and Agra childhood, the journey to Calcutta and the quarrel with its poets, his imprisonment for gambling, his years at the court of Bahadur Shah, the Revolt of 1857 and Dastambu, the Qati'-e Burhan controversy, and then a long portrait of his character: his wit, generosity, pride, drinking, faith, friendships, home life, last illness and death, with the anecdotes that every later account of Ghalib repeats. The main early source for Ghalib's life and for literary Delhi before and after 1857. Complete Urdu text from the first edition (Nami Press, Kanpur, 1897), with a facing English translation of the prose and of all the Persian and Urdu verse, an introduction and a glossary. Part Two, Hali's anthology of Ghalib's verse and prose, is not included.
translation_note: Faithful English translation made for this library, section by section, with translator's notes marked [TN]. Each reading section is one chapter, ending with a glossary.
